newsitem.title: UK: London gold closes firmer, steadies near resistance.
newsitem.headline: London gold closes firmer, steadies near resistance.

text.p: Gold prices continued to hover around $380 per ounce on Friday after showing little response to events elsewhere in financial markets.
"It looks as though it could hang around here, which would be disappointing, as there should be some more movement left in the price," one dealer said.
Gold ended at $380.45 per ounce, having closed on Thursday at $379.25.
Dealers reported light two-way business but said the market was generally quiet and defensive. However, one said: "It is behaving as if it could move either way quite sharply."
Gold showed little if any reaction to a surprise fall of 40,000 jobs in September U.S. payrolls after economists had forecast a rise of 166,000.
The jobless rate was marked up to 5.2 percent from 5.1 percent in August, combining with the payroll data to send debt futures soaring but causing the dollar to dip.
However, the moves did not follow through to the precious sector. "The figures had no effect on gold," one dealer said.
Lending rates were a little easier as the spot price moved to the top end of its current $377-$380 range, indicating some lending was coming in at the higher levels and taking the pressure off rates.

The gold price has been struggling to get back over $380 for over a week since speculative investment funds became impatient with a dull precious metals sector and sold their gold holdings in favour of the better profit potential of the stock and bond markets.
Silver was unchanged at $4.91 and was seen following gold, which was attracting most attention.
"It's been very quiet and is stuck in a $4.85-$4.95 range," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were both firmer but quiet with platinum at $384.40, up $1.20, and palladium $0.75 ahead at $120.50.
